A4.name: FRC.Subject.frame_web
A4.doc: 7:A4, 7:A17, **C1 (p00021), the frame's web.** On every frame, `π = 2κ` and `i = −g^κ`: `2π ≡ −1`, `g^π = −1`, `−π = 2⁻¹`, `i² = −1`; `0` and `1` are squares and the drive is not, the one nonsquare frame datum.

A6.name: FRC.Subject.signature
A6.doc: 7:A6, **C3 (p00150), the Euclidean–Lorentzian dichotomy.** On every frame the temporal coefficient `ν = g` is a nonsquare; the norm form `x² − ν t²` has a zero with `t ≠ 0` iff `ν` is a square (split torus) and none otherwise (non-split); `ν = 2⁻¹ · (2g)`, and the classes of `2⁻¹` and `2g` are fixed by the parity of `κ`.

A6.name: FRC.Subject.half_class
A6.doc: 7:A6, 7:A16, The Carrier's class `[c²] = [2⁻¹]` (C3, C8): on a prime `p = 4S + 1`, the half `h` (`2h = 1`) is a square iff `S` is even; the half is `2S + 1` (`Prime.half_square_iff`).

A9.name: FRC.Lorentz.similitude

A13.name: FRC.Spin.ad_preserves
A13.doc: 7:A13, 7:D1, 00:C22 — conjugation `X ↦ M X adj(M)` multiplies the determinant by `det(M)²` and the trace by `det M`: on `SL₂` it preserves `−det` on the trace-zero matrices — the map `PGL₂(𝔽_p) → SO₃(𝔽_p)` of the row.

A13.name: FRC.Spin.ad_kernel
A13.doc: 7:A13, 00:C22 — the kernel of the adjoint action is the centre: on a frame (an odd shell) a matrix commuting with `J` and with `D` is scalar, `b = c = 0` and `a = d`; so `PGL₂ → SO₃` is injective.

A14.name: FRC.Spin.hermitian_wJ
A14.doc: 7:A14, 00:C27 — the form `wJ` is Hermitian: `(wJ)† = wJ`, because `conj w = −w` (`w^p = −w`) and `Jᵀ = −J`.

A14.name: FRC.Spin.su2_eq_sl2
A14.doc: 7:A14, 7:D1, 00:C27 — **the frame group has one form.** On a field shell, `ν` a nonsquare and `w ≠ 0` (the form `wJ` is Hermitian for `conj w = −w`, `hermitian_wJ`): a matrix over `𝔽_{p²}` of determinant one is unitary for `wJ` exactly when its entries are fixed by the Frobenius conjugation, i.e. lie in `𝔽_p` — `SU₂(𝔽_{p²}/𝔽_p) = SL₂(𝔽_p)`.

A14.name: FRC.Spin.finite_order
A14.doc: 7:A14, 7:C9, 00:C27 — every element of `SL₂` has finite order: with `det M = 1` some positive `n ≤ p⁴` has `Mⁿ = I` — the `p⁴ + 1` powers `M⁰, …, M^{p⁴}` cannot be distinct, and the adjugate cancels the common factor.

A15.name: FRC.Subject.torus_antipode
A15.doc: 7:A15, **C25 (p00139), the antipode `[1 : 0]` is `−1` on the boost torus.** On a prime `p = 4κ + 1` with `ν` a nonsquare and `𝔽_{p²} = 𝔽_p[w]/(w² − ν)`: a direction `[x : y] ≠ 0` has the boost `u = yν + xw` of nonzero norm, and `v = a + bw` moves it by `q ↦ (aq + νb)/(bq + a)`; the torsor map `u ↦ u/ū` lands on `C_{p+1}`, is constant on the classes `𝔽_p^× u` and equivariant, and is a bijection from the directions onto `C_{p+1}`; it sends the origin `[0 : 1]` to `1` and the antipode `[1 : 0]` to `−1`, the one element of order two, and `𝔽_p^× ∩ C_{p+1} = {±1}`; the one boost of order two is the class of `w`, `q ↦ ν/q`, which swaps the origin and the antipode; and `2s = 0` forces `s = 0`, the seam `2κ + (2κ + 1) = 0`: `2⁻¹ = 2κ + 1 = −2κ`.

A15.name: FRC.Subject.antipode_generator
A15.doc: 7:A15, 00:C25, 22:P4 — the antipode is `ζ^{(p+1)/2}` for every generator `ζ` of the torus: a norm-one `ζ` of order exactly `p + 1` has `ζ^{2κ+1} = −1`, the torus's one element of order two.

A15.name: FRC.Subject.boost_unique
A15.doc: 7:A15, 00:C25 — `u_P` is the unique boost carrying the origin to `P`: a boost `v` with `v · dir(0, 1) = c · dir(x, y)` is `(c/ν) · dir(x, y)`, so it is `dir(x, y)` up to a scalar, which acts trivially on `ℙ¹` and leaves the ratio unchanged.

A16.name: FRC.Subject.square_class
A16.doc: 7:A16, **C8 (p00028), the square class is chronon parity.** On every frame `g^m` is a square iff `m` is even: the registered (two-way) transport `g²` is even, the one-way multiplier `g` and its inverse odd.

A16.name: FRC.Shell.Prime.tsirelson
A16.doc: 7:A16, 00:C8, 22:C17, 22:C25, 22:X7, 22:P3 — the Tsirelson square without a generator: `ζ⁴ = −1` gives `(ζ + ζ⁷)² = 2`.

A17.doc: 7:F5, 7:X6, 7:F4, 7:A17 — **a count below the Carrier's cycle is its own residue**: the chart count of a duration `n < Ω − 1` is `n`.

A17.name: FRC.Lorentz.nesting_depth

A17.name: FRC.Lorentz.drift_instance_pairs
A17.doc: 7:F4, 7:A17 — the three laboratory pairs and `(13, 181)`: `p² < Ω − 1` on each, and the hosted joint periods all exceed `p²`.

A21.name: FRC.Drift.nesting_bound
A21.doc: 7:A21, 38:C13 — **the apsidal bound is the nesting condition.** A nested Subject `p = q + 1` on a Carrier `Ω` registers the apsidal fraction `κ/S = (p − 1)/(Ω − 1)` (`Pair.leak_rate`), and the bound `κ/S < 1/(√Ω + 1)` is, squared and cleared of its root, `(p − 1)²Ω < (Ω − p)²`, which holds exactly when `p² < Ω`: with `Ω = p² + d`, `(Ω − p)² − (p − 1)²Ω = d(Ω − 1) > 0` for `d ≥ 1`, and with `p² = Ω + d`, `Ω = m + q + 1`, `(Ω − p)² + d(Ω − 1) = (p − 1)²Ω`, so the bound fails. On the physical Carrier no hosted Subject registers an observed precession (the paper's C13).

A21.name: FRC.Pair.leak_rate
A21.doc: 7:A21, 7:A24, 7:A25, 7:F1, 38:C10, 38:C7, 38:C13, 38:C14, 38:X1, 38:X3 — the leak rate per chronon is `κ`-free: `(κ/S)/(p − 1) = 1/(4S) = 1/(Ω − 1)`, as the integer identities `κ · 4S = S · (p − 1)`, `4S = Ω − 1`, and the temporal face on the cover `2(Ω − 1) = 8S`.

A23.name: FRC.Shell.Prime.isPrime_iff_complete
A23.doc: 7:A23, Completeness is primality, in the ideal form (A10): for `p ≥ 2`, every ideal of the shell that holds a nonzero residue holds every residue iff `p` is prime. An ideal `I` holds `0` and is closed under addition and under multiplication by any residue. Forward, a nonzero `a ∈ I` has the inverse `a^{p−2}` (Fermat), so `1 ∈ I` and then `x = x · 1 ∈ I`. Backward, the annihilator `{x : x b = 0}` of `b` is an ideal, so `a b = 0` with `a ≠ 0` puts `1` in it and `b = 0`: no zero divisors, so `p` is prime.

A25.name: FRC.Pair.joint_cycle
A25.doc: 7:A25, 38:C14, 38:B5, 38:B7 — the joint cycle of a `κ`-odd pair with `S` even: `κ = 2a + 1`, `S = 2m`, `ℓ` a common multiple of `2a + 1` and `m` with `ℓ/m` odd (`ℓ = (2a + 1)(2u + 1) = m(2v + 1)`). At `4ℓ` ticks the shell is home (`4ℓ ≡ 0 mod 4κ`) and the Carrier reads the half (`4ℓ ≡ 4m = (Ω − 1)/2 mod 8m`); at `8ℓ` both are home. At the instance `ℓ = 87 = 3 · 29`.

A25.name: FRC.Pair.joint_cycle_frame
A25.doc: 7:A25, 38:C14 on the frames: a Subject frame of odd capacity `κ = 2a + 1` and a Carrier frame of even capacity `S = 2m` return together — at `4ℓ` the Subject's drive is home, `g^{4ℓ} = 1`, and the Carrier's reads the half, `h^{4ℓ} = −1` (the sign event); at `8ℓ` both are home.

A25.name: FRC.Pair.joint_return_iff
A25.doc: 7:A25, 38:C14 — the joint returns are exactly the common multiples of the two periods, so the least is `lcm(p − 1, Ω − 1)`; for `κ` odd and `S = 2m` even it is `8ℓ`, `ℓ` the least common multiple of `κ` and `m` (`joint_return_eight`), whose cofactor over `m` is odd (`joint_cycle_frame`).

A25.name: FRC.Pair.joint_return_eight
A25.doc: 7:A25, 38:C14 — every common multiple of the periods `4κ` (`κ = 2a + 1` odd) and `8m` (`S = 2m` even) is eight times a common multiple of `κ` and `m`: with `joint_return_iff` the least joint return is `8ℓ`, `ℓ = lcm(κ, m)`, and its half `4ℓ` is `joint_cycle_frame`'s sign event (`ℓ/m = κ/gcd(κ, m)` is odd).

A25.name: FRC.Pair.recurrence
A25.doc: 7:A25, 38:B5, 38:C14 — the recurrence data at the instance: `696 = lcm(12, 232) = 58·12 = 3·232` is the least common return, `1392 = 2·696` the spinor recurrence; the joint cycle's `ℓ = 87 = 3·29`: at `4ℓ = 348` the shell is home (`348 ≡ 0 mod 12`) and the Carrier reads the half (`348 ≡ 116 mod 232`, `78³⁴⁸ = −1`), at `8ℓ = 696` both are home.

A26.name: FRC.Pair.tick_home
A26.doc: 7:A26, 38:C1, 38:C5 — home: at the row's own clock the count is `0`.

A26.name: FRC.Pair.flow_stations
A26.doc: 7:A26, 38:C1, 38:C5, 38:D1 — the flow law as tick counts on `C₂₃₂` (`tick`): row `k` is home at `b_C = k` and at its parity image (`116`) at `b_C = 116 + k`, for every row; the count returns the row at every clock state.

A28.name: FRC.Drift.conj_branch
A28.doc: 7:A28, 21:C3, 21:C10, 00:E3 — the single arrow: on the norm-one circle `N(z) = 1`, `zⁿ · (conj z)ⁿ = 1` for every `n`, so the conjugate (Frobenius) branch of a clock is its orbit run backwards (`conj (zⁿ)` inverts `zⁿ`, with `conj_pow`): a time-reversed clock is the conjugation, not a step of the drive — the row's reading is that a repulsive source would need that branch.

A28.name: FRC.Drift.conj_pow
A28.doc: 7:A28, 21:C3, 00:E3 — the conjugate of a power is the power of the conjugate, `conj (zⁿ) = (conj z)ⁿ`, on `𝔽_p[w]/(w² − ν)`.

B1.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.Fld.hopf_section
B1.doc: 7:B1, 7:C7, 7:P1, 38:A7, 38:A9 — **C19 (p00039), the Hopf section.** In `PGL₂(𝔽_p)` on a frame, `ν` a nonsquare: (1) a boost that is not scalar fixes no point of `ℙ¹`; (2) a boost in the Borel subgroup is scalar: `T ∩ B = 1`; (3) every invertible matrix factors as (cone chart) × (boost) up to a scalar, (4) uniquely up to scalars — the cone chart is a global section of `G → G/T`; (5) the boost classes are the points of `ℙ¹` (`p + 1` per fibre) and (6) the cone charts number `p (p − 1)`; (7) on the spin cover `SL₂` the sign `−I` is both a boost and a chart, `B ∩ T = {±I}` there, and `b t = (−b)(−t)`: the section obstructs at `−1`.

B1.name: FRC.Lorentz.consecutive_orders
B1.doc: 7:P1, 7:B1 — the three cycles have the consecutive orders `4κ`, `4κ + 1`, `4κ + 2` on the shell `p = 4κ + 1`.

B1.name: FRC.Lorentz.minus_one_in_both
B1.doc: 7:B1, 7:C7 — on the spin cover `−I` is both upper triangular of determinant one and a norm-one diagonal matrix `diag(λ, λ̄)`: the Borel lift and the torus lift meet in `±I`, the obstruction to a subgroup section.

B4.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.Fld.norm_ne_zero
B4.doc: 7:B4, 38:A9, 00:C19 — on a field-law shell, `x² − ν y² ≠ 0` for `(x, y) ≠ 0` when `ν` is a nonsquare.

B4.name: FRC.Lorentz.register_elliptic
B4.doc: 7:B4, 7:X1, 7:C5 — **the register square is elliptic**: on a field shell with `ν` a nonsquare, two null points `u u†`, `v v†` whose sum is null have proportional vectors, `u₁ v₂ = u₂ v₁`: the null cone contains no totally isotropic plane.

B4.name: FRC.Lorentz.frame_hyperbolic
B4.doc: 7:B4, 7:X1, 7:C5 — **the frame quadric is hyperbolic**: the matrices `[[a, b], [0, 0]]` form a totally isotropic plane of `det` on `M₂(𝔽_p)`.

B6.name: FRC.Register.translation_fixes_antipode
B6.doc: 7:B6 — **a nontrivial translation fixes the antipode alone.** On the frame's line the translation `[x : y] ↦ [x + by : y]` with `b ≠ 0` fixes `[x : y]` exactly when `y = 0`: `x + by = x` forces `by = 0`, and the prime shell has no zero divisors.

C1.name: FRC.Lorentz.register_det
C1.doc: 7:C1 — `det X(x) = x₀² − x₁² − x₃² + ν x₂²`.

C1.name: FRC.Lorentz.time_vector
C1.doc: 7:C1, 7:D1 — the time vector `X(0, 0, 1, 0)` is the Hermitian form `ηJ` of 00:C27 (`Theme/Spin.lean`).

C2.name: FRC.Lorentz.congruence_det
C2.doc: 7:C2 — the congruence multiplies the determinant by the norm of `det A`: `det(A X A†) = det A · conj(det A) · det X`.

C2.name: FRC.Lorentz.congruence_hermitian
C2.doc: 7:C2 — the congruence of a Hermitian matrix is Hermitian.

C2.name: FRC.Lorentz.congruence_preserves
C2.doc: 7:F3, 7:C2 — a congruence of determinant one preserves the form: `det(A X A†) = det X` when `det A = 1`.

C2.name: FRC.Lorentz.kernel_pm
C2.doc: 7:X4, 7:C2 — **the kernel of the congruence is `±I`**: a matrix of determinant one fixing the four basis vectors of the register square is `I` or `−I`.

C3.name: FRC.Lorentz.cone_point
C3.doc: 7:C3 — the Hermitian matrix of `v = (v₁, v₂)`: `v v† = X(x)` with `x₀ = h(N v₁ + N v₂)`, `x₃ = h(N v₁ − N v₂)` (`2h = 1`), `(x₁, x₂) = v₁ conj v₂`, and `Q(x) = 0`: a null point of the register square.

C3.name: FRC.Lorentz.null_count_13
C3.doc: 7:C3, 7:C4 — **the cone by vectors at `p = 13`**: `2041 = p³ − p² + p` null vectors, hence `(2041 − 1)/12 = 170 = p² + 1` null lines, the count of `cone_count_13`.

C4.name: FRC.Lorentz.cone_time
C4.doc: 7:C4 — a direction `[z : 1]` with `z ∉ 𝔽_p` carries a time component: the `x₂` coordinate of `v v†`, `v = (z, 1)`, is `Im z`.

C4.name: FRC.Lorentz.null_count_13
C4.doc: 7:C3, 7:C4 — **the cone by vectors at `p = 13`**: `2041 = p³ − p² + p` null vectors, hence `(2041 − 1)/12 = 170 = p² + 1` null lines, the count of `cone_count_13`.

C4.name: FRC.Lorentz.cone_count_13
C4.doc: 7:C4 — the cone's `p² + 1` directions are the `p + 1` of space and the `p(p − 1)` causal rays, at `p = 13`.

C5.name: FRC.Lorentz.rank_two_det
C5.doc: 7:C5 — the determinant of a sum of two rank-one Hermitian matrices is the norm of the two-by-two determinant of the vectors: `det(u u† + v v†) = N(u₁ v₂ − u₂ v₁)`.

C5.name: FRC.Lorentz.register_elliptic
C5.doc: 7:B4, 7:X1, 7:C5 — **the register square is elliptic**: on a field shell with `ν` a nonsquare, two null points `u u†`, `v v†` whose sum is null have proportional vectors, `u₁ v₂ = u₂ v₁`: the null cone contains no totally isotropic plane.

C5.name: FRC.Lorentz.frame_hyperbolic
C5.doc: 7:B4, 7:X1, 7:C5 — **the frame quadric is hyperbolic**: the matrices `[[a, b], [0, 0]]` form a totally isotropic plane of `det` on `M₂(𝔽_p)`.

C6.name: FRC.Lorentz.similitude
C6.doc: 7:A9, 7:X5, 7:C6 — with `a² + b² = ν`, the map `(x₀, x₁, x₂, x₃) ↦ (ν x₂, a x₁ − b x₃, x₀, b x₁ + a x₃)` multiplies the form by `ν`: `⟨1, 1, 1, ν⟩ ≅ ⟨1, ν, ν, ν⟩`, a similitude of multiplier `ν` exchanging the two non-null classes.

C6.name: FRC.Lorentz.two_squares
C6.doc: 7:C6 — on a shell with a quarter-turn `i² = −1` and `2h = 1`, every `ν` is a sum of two squares: `ν = ((ν + 1)h)² + (i(ν − 1)h)²`.

C7.name: FRC.Lorentz.ray_stabiliser
C7.doc: 7:C7 — the stabiliser of the ray `η` in the frame moves: `[[a, b], [c, d]]` fixes `η` under `z ↦ (az + b)/(cz + d)`, i.e. `aη + b = (cη + d)η`, exactly when `a = d` and `b = νc`: the norm-one torus `[[a, νc], [c, a]]` of A10.

C7.name: FRC.Lorentz.minus_one_in_both
C7.doc: 7:B1, 7:C7 — on the spin cover `−I` is both upper triangular of determinant one and a norm-one diagonal matrix `diag(λ, λ̄)`: the Borel lift and the torus lift meet in `±I`, the obstruction to a subgroup section.

C7.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.Fld.hopf_section
C7.doc: 7:B1, 7:C7, 7:P1, 38:A7, 38:A9 — **C19 (p00039), the Hopf section.** In `PGL₂(𝔽_p)` on a frame, `ν` a nonsquare: (1) a boost that is not scalar fixes no point of `ℙ¹`; (2) a boost in the Borel subgroup is scalar: `T ∩ B = 1`; (3) every invertible matrix factors as (cone chart) × (boost) up to a scalar, (4) uniquely up to scalars — the cone chart is a global section of `G → G/T`; (5) the boost classes are the points of `ℙ¹` (`p + 1` per fibre) and (6) the cone charts number `p (p − 1)`; (7) on the spin cover `SL₂` the sign `−I` is both a boost and a chart, `B ∩ T = {±I}` there, and `b t = (−b)(−t)`: the section obstructs at `−1`.

C8.name: FRC.Lorentz.axis_discriminant
C8.doc: 7:X2, 7:C8, 7:C10 — the axis of a ray `z`: the binary form `(t − z)(t − z̄) = t² − tr(z) t + N(z)` has discriminant `tr(z)² − 4 N(z) = ν (2 Im z)²`, a nonsquare times a square.

C9.name: FRC.Lorentz.class_partition_13
C9.doc: 7:C9, 7:X2 — **the class equation by elements at `p = 13`.** The `26208` invertible matrices fall into the three discriminant classes with `12012`, `2028` and `12168` elements; divided by the `12` scalars these are the `1001` split classes, the identity with the `168` unipotent classes, and the `1014` non-split classes of `PGL₂(𝔽₁₃)`: the three terms of `class_equation_13`.

C9.name: FRC.Spin.finite_order
C9.doc: 7:A14, 7:C9, 00:C27 — every element of `SL₂` has finite order: with `det M = 1` some positive `n ≤ p⁴` has `Mⁿ = I` — the `p⁴ + 1` powers `M⁰, …, M^{p⁴}` cannot be distinct, and the adjugate cancels the common factor.

C10.name: FRC.Register.fixed_points_13
C10.doc: 7:C10 — **the fixed points by the discriminant class at `p = 13`.** Every non-identity element of `PGL₂(𝔽₁₃)` fixes the predicted number of directions; the tally `1001`, `168`, `1014` of two, one and none is the class equation's three terms.

C10.name: FRC.Register.fixed_points_of_class
C10.doc: 7:C10 — **the three kinds of cycle are the three kinds of direction at `p = 13`.** `14` null directions, `78` nonsquare and `91` square axes; the tally of `fixed_points_13` is `78 · 13` elements with no fixed point (the non-split tori, `13` non-identity elements each), `14 · 12` with one (the unipotent groups, `12` each) and `91 · 11` with two (the split tori, `11` each).

C10.name: FRC.Lorentz.axis_discriminant
C10.doc: 7:X2, 7:C8, 7:C10 — the axis of a ray `z`: the binary form `(t − z)(t − z̄) = t² − tr(z) t + N(z)` has discriminant `tr(z)² − 4 N(z) = ν (2 Im z)²`, a nonsquare times a square.

D1.name: FRC.Spin.su2_eq_sl2
D1.doc: 7:A14, 7:D1, 00:C27 — **the frame group has one form.** On a field shell, `ν` a nonsquare and `w ≠ 0` (the form `wJ` is Hermitian for `conj w = −w`, `hermitian_wJ`): a matrix over `𝔽_{p²}` of determinant one is unitary for `wJ` exactly when its entries are fixed by the Frobenius conjugation, i.e. lie in `𝔽_p` — `SU₂(𝔽_{p²}/𝔽_p) = SL₂(𝔽_p)`.

D1.name: FRC.Lorentz.time_vector
D1.doc: 7:C1, 7:D1 — the time vector `X(0, 0, 1, 0)` is the Hermitian form `ηJ` of 00:C27 (`Theme/Spin.lean`).

D1.name: FRC.Spin.ad_preserves
D1.doc: 7:A13, 7:D1, 00:C22 — conjugation `X ↦ M X adj(M)` multiplies the determinant by `det(M)²` and the trace by `det M`: on `SL₂` it preserves `−det` on the trace-zero matrices — the map `PGL₂(𝔽_p) → SO₃(𝔽_p)` of the row.

D3.name: FRC.Lorentz.drive_time
D3.doc: 7:D3, 7:A16 — the one-chronon move `diag(g, 1)` carries the time vector `ηJ = X(0, 0, 1, 0)` to `g·ηJ = X(0, 0, g, 0)`: its square class flips with the chronon parity, and it carries the ray `(z, 1)` to `(gz, 1)`.

D3.name: FRC.Lorentz.lift_det
D3.doc: 7:D3 — the unimodular lift `D = diag(η, uη)`, `νu = 1` (so `uη = η⁻¹`), has determinant one.

D3.name: FRC.Lorentz.lift_time
D3.doc: 7:D3 — the lift negates the time vector: `D (ηJ) D† = −ηJ`, i.e. `X(0, 0, 1, 0) ↦ X(0, 0, −1, 0)`.

D3.name: FRC.Lorentz.even_transport
D3.doc: 7:D3 — the even transport `diag(g, u)`, `gu = 1`, fixes the time vector and `σ_x` and dilates `E₂₂` by `u²` and `E₁₁` by `g²`.

D4.name: FRC.Lorentz.neg_one_trivial
D4.doc: 7:X4, 7:D4 — `−I` acts trivially on the register square: the spinor's two circuits are one on the square.

D4.name: FRC.Lorentz.torus_conjugate
D4.doc: 7:D4 — `P diag(λ, λ̄) = (mult λ) P` for `P = [[η, −η], [1, 1]]` and `mult λ = [[x, νy], [y, x]]`, `λ = x + yη`: the norm-one diagonal group `N¹` and the torus lift are conjugate in `SL₂(K)` through `P`.

D5.name: FRC.Spacetime.isotropic_three
D5.doc: 7:D5 — **no definite space**: for every prime shell `p`, every `ν` and any three vectors `u, v, w` of `𝔽_p⁴`, some nonzero coefficient triple gives a null vector of the determinant form `x₀² − x₁² − x₃² + ν x₂²` in their span — every three-dimensional subspace of the register square contains a null vector (`FRC.Lorentz.isotropic_three`, `Theme/Lorentz.lean`, by Chevalley–Warning).

D6.name: FRC.Lorentz.antipode_order_two
D6.doc: 7:D6, 7:A15 — `η` has order two modulo `𝔽_p^×`: `η² = ν ∈ 𝔽_p` while `η ∉ 𝔽_p` (its imaginary part is `1`).

D6.name: FRC.Lorentz.half_step_odd
D6.doc: 7:D6 — the half step of the cycle `C_{p+1}`, `p = 4κ + 1`: `p + 1 = 2(2κ + 1)`, and `2κ + 1` is odd.

D6.name: FRC.Lorentz.even_never_antipode
D6.doc: 7:D6 — **the even steps never reach the antipode.** On a field shell with a quarter-turn `i² = −1` and `ν` a nonsquare, no square `y²` of the extension lies on the line `𝔽_p^× η` of the antipode: `y² = cη`, `c ≠ 0`, would make `ν = (i · N(y) · c⁻¹)²` a square. The unimodular torus, the even powers of a generator, misses the antipode.

D6.name: FRC.Lorentz.antipode_half_step_13
D6.doc: 7:D6 — **the antipode at the odd half step, by every generator, at `p = 13`.** `K^×/𝔽₁₃^×` is a cycle of order `14` with `6 = φ(14)` generators, and every generator first carries the origin `η = [0 : 1]` to the antipode `1 = [1 : 0]` at the step `7 = (p + 1)/2 = 2κ + 1`, which is odd; `η` itself has order two.

F1.name: FRC.Pair.leak_rate
F1.doc: 7:A21, 7:A24, 7:A25, 7:F1, 38:C10, 38:C7, 38:C13, 38:C14, 38:X1, 38:X3 — the leak rate per chronon is `κ`-free: `(κ/S)/(p − 1) = 1/(4S) = 1/(Ω − 1)`, as the integer identities `κ · 4S = S · (p − 1)`, `4S = Ω − 1`, and the temporal face on the cover `2(Ω − 1) = 8S`.

F3.name: FRC.Lorentz.no_time_reversal
F3.doc: 7:X6, 7:F3 — **the time reversal is not a Lorentz move.** No matrix of determinant one carries the four basis vectors of the register square as the Frobenius does, `x₂ ↦ −x₂` (which negates the time vector and fixes `I`, `σ_x`, `σ_z`).

F3.name: FRC.Lorentz.no_reflection
F3.doc: 7:X6, 7:F3 — **a spatial reflection is not a Lorentz move**: no matrix of determinant one carries the basis as `x₁ ↦ −x₁` (negating `σ_x`, fixing `I`, `σ_z` and the time vector).

F3.name: FRC.Lorentz.no_inversion
F3.doc: 7:X6, 7:F3 — **the total inversion is not a Lorentz move**: no matrix of determinant one carries the basis as `X ↦ −X`.

F4.name: FRC.Lorentz.drift_one_directional
F4.doc: 7:F5, 7:X6, 7:F4, 7:A17 — **a count below the Carrier's cycle is its own residue**: the chart count of a duration `n < Ω − 1` is `n`.

F4.name: FRC.Lorentz.nesting_depth
F4.doc: 7:F5, 7:B5, 7:F4, 7:A17 — **the nesting bound keeps every registrable depth below the cycle.** For an odd `p` with `p² < Ω = 4S + 1`, `p²` is odd and `4S` even, so `p² ≤ 4S − 1`, and a registered duration `n ≤ p²` has `n < Ω − 1`: the cycle never acts.

F4.name: FRC.Lorentz.drift_instance_pairs
F4.doc: 7:F4, 7:A17 — the three laboratory pairs and `(13, 181)`: `p² < Ω − 1` on each, and the hosted joint periods all exceed `p²`.

F4.name: FRC.Lorentz.joint_period
F4.doc: 7:F4, 7:A25 — the joint period of a coprime pair, with its Bezout certificate `aκ = bS + 1` (at the laboratory pair `(13, 233)`: `3 · 39 = 2 · 58 + 1`): `4κS` is a common multiple of `4κ` and `4S`, and every common multiple `L = 4κx = 4Sy` is a multiple of `4κS` — the joint period is `lcm(4κ, 4S) = 4κS`.

F4.name: FRC.Lorentz.drift_injective
F4.doc: 7:X6, 7:F4 — **the drift distinguishes the revolutions on a hosted pair.** For a coprime pair, with its Bezout certificate `aκ = bS + 1`, the chart count `4κn mod 4S` of the shell's origin after `n` revolutions is injective on `n < S`: two revolutions below `S` at the same chart count are the same revolution.

F4.name: FRC.Lorentz.drift_injective_gcd
F4.doc: 7:F4 — **the drift distinguishes the revolutions, general hosted pair.** With `d = gcd(κ, S)`, `κ = d κ'`, `S = d S'` and a Bezout certificate `a κ' = b S' + 1` for the coprime parts, the chart count `4κn mod 4S` is injective on `n < S' = S/d`.

F4.name: FRC.Lorentz.drift_instance_gcd
F4.doc: 7:F4 — an admissible pair with `gcd(κ, S) = 3`: `(13, 181)`, `κ = 3 · 1`, `S = 45 = 3 · 15`, the certificate `1 · 1 = 0 · 15 + 1` for the coprime parts, and the joint period `lcm(12, 180) = 180 = 4κS/3`.

F5.name: FRC.Register.record_second_law
F5.doc: 7:F5 — **the record is strictly increasing below the cycle.** For `n < m < Ω − 1` the chart counts are `n` and `m` themselves, so the record of `m` chronons holds the record of `n` and one entry more per chronon, the entries distinct.

F5.name: FRC.Register.record_quarter

F5.name: FRC.Register.record_quarter_pairs
F5.doc: 7:F5 — **the three laboratory pairs**: `p² = 4κ(p + 1) + 1` at `p = 13, 173, 1549`, and `p² < Ω − 1` in the Carriers `233, 30089, 2408561`, so the record saturates below the cycle.

P2.name: FRC.Register.floor_is_temperature
P2.doc: 7:P2 — **the floor is the Carrier's temperature.** With the chart's unit `k_B c = ħ` (00:B7), `k_B · (cH) = ħ · H`: the de Sitter temperature `ħH/(2π k_B)` and the floor `cH/2π` are one number, `k_B T_dS = (ħ/c) a₀`.
